title: India–US trade deal: announced in February, still not signed
dek: A tariff cut was announced with fanfare. Nine months later, courts, new duties and a sanctions law have kept it in limbo.
bigLabel: US duty on most Indian goods since 24 Jul

glance.what: The US and India announced a deal in February to cut US tariffs on Indian goods to 18% from 50%. On 18 November India's Commerce Secretary said the deal is "more or less finalised" but cannot be signed until the US sets its new tariff structure.
glance.why: US tariffs decide how competitive Indian exports like textiles, gems, engineering goods and pharma are in India’s biggest export market.
glance.next: Signing waits on Washington's new tariff rules and pending Section 301 investigations, per the Commerce Secretary. A former senior US diplomat says both sides may aim to close phase one around the G20 summit in Florida next month.

forYou: If you work in or invest in export-heavy sectors, the final tariff rate matters more than the headlines. Nothing announced is binding until a deal is signed.

events.title: Trump announces a deal: tariffs to 18% from 50%
events.summary: In return, India is to stop buying Russian oil and lower trade barriers for US goods.

events.title: Joint statement sets out a framework for an interim deal
events.summary: Both governments publish a framework for an interim agreement, with talks on a wider trade pact to follow.

events.title: US Supreme Court strikes down the legal basis for the tariffs
events.summary: In a 6–3 ruling, the court says the emergency-powers law (IEEPA) does not authorise tariffs. The US turns to other trade laws.

events.title: A new 10% duty on most Indian goods
events.summary: A Section 301 duty of 10% starts applying to most Indian imports into the US, becoming the main sticking point in talks.

events.title: US sanctions law threatens tariffs of up to 100%
events.summary: A new US law authorises tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, naming India and China as at direct risk.

events.title: Still no signed deal
events.summary: The 18% rate announced in February was never applied. After the US midterms, Indian trade analysts argue an early interim deal has become more likely.

events.title: Goyal: India will have one of the 'best' deals
events.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says India has negotiated a very good set of outcomes, while changes in US tariffs have led to further talks. Sources say the US midterm results will not affect the interim deal. A former US diplomat says both sides may aim to close phase one by the G20 summit next month.

events.title: Commerce Secretary: deal 'more or less finalised' but can't be signed until new US tariff rules are in place
events.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said "every aspect of the deal has been more or less finalised" and negotiations will conclude soon. But he said the two countries cannot sign it until Washington puts its new tariff structure in place: "Till that tariff architecture is in place, the countries won't be able to sign the deal." The US is rebuilding its tariffs after its Supreme Court ruled in February that the emergency law used for the earlier tariffs did not allow them. Agrawal also pointed to pending US Section 301 investigations, saying countries will want to know their outcome before signing. He spoke at a FICCI event in New Delhi, per ANI.

events.title: Farmers' groups plan protests on 26 November against the US trade deal
events.summary: The Samyukta Kisan Morcha, a coalition of farmers' unions, says farmers will march in Delhi, from Mandir Marg to Jantar Mantar, and protest at about 100 other places on 26 November. They want India to drop the proposed trade deal with the US and other free trade agreements. Farm leaders say cheaper US farm imports would hurt Indian farmers. The government has not announced a signing date.
